items.text: SEASON 10 · EPISODE 8 · DRAFT  Coldframe Sound · week five · Maya, Esme, Hollis, Corbin and Pim · Level L6 · Mastery support (reference only — choose the tool and say why)  A stranger sends Esme her own unreleased vocal, remixed. By lunchtime there’s a second question, worse than the first: what else of her voice is the label asking for?  ⚑ RV-176: her performance, her call. RV-179: consent and recordings — not legal advice. RV-177: figures illustrative. Some choices run on a clock — and some depend on your loadout.

items.title: Her Voice
items.stakes: An unreleased vocal is out in the world, and a contract rider wants the rest of her voice.
items.clock: Before the label's lawyers call at five.
items.reward: The leak stopped and told truthfully — and nothing of hers leaving without her yes.

objectives.text: Decide the answer to the rider
Decide how files leave the building

items.text: Cold open — “Doing things I never sang”

items.alt: The control room; Esme stands with her arms wrapped round herself, her phone in one hand; Maya faces her, calm.

bubbles.text: It's my voice. On a stranger's phone. Doing things I never sang.
First we stop it going further. Then I tell you everything we know, and everything we don't.

items.prompt: 11:05. An unreleased vocal is out. Esme is shaking. What first?
items.risk: More copies every hour — or a story told for her.

hints.text: What's yours to stop, and what's hers to say?

options.label: Post a statement from the studio's account
options.result: Esme: “Not your words. Not about my voice.”
options.consequence: Speaks for her before she's decided what to say.
options.fail: What's said publicly about her voice is hers and the label's to decide.

options.label: Disable the link now and keep its access log; find exactly what it pointed at; then tell Esme and Hollis what went out, when — and what you don't know
options.result: Link dead. 38 downloads from 11 addresses over 16 days; the folder held nine vocal stems. Esme: “Thank you for not making it smaller than it is.”
options.consequence: Stop the exposure, keep the evidence, tell the truth to the person it's about.

options.label: Find the stranger online and demand they delete it
options.result: Corbin: “The label's lawyers do that. The studio doesn't go after a person.”
options.consequence: Not yours — and a private person is not a target.

options.label: Say nothing until you know more
options.result: The link stays open another afternoon. Six more downloads.

items.title: Anyone with the link.
items.body: The label's rough-mix review link was set to ‘anyone with the link — can download — no expiry’, and it pointed at the whole folder: eleven mixes and, in a subfolder nobody remembered, nine vocal stems. Open for sixteen days. Thirty-eight downloads from eleven addresses. The studio can put a name to three.
items.label: Test: how much of it can you account for?

items.title: ‘Anyone with the link · Can download’
items.body: The file share's settings page, screenshotted before the link was disabled: ‘Anyone with the link — Can download — No expiry.’ Created by the label's review account, sixteen days ago.

items.title: A roll of paper and a song
items.body: In 1908 the U.S. Supreme Court decided that a paper roll for a player piano wasn't a ‘copy’ of the song punched into it — so the songwriter's publisher had no say over it. Congress answered the next year with a copyright law that gave composers rights over machines playing their music. Every new machine since has reopened the same question: who decides what's done with a performance?

items.title: The rider.
items.body: Corbin comes in with a printout and doesn't sit down. The label's new rider, sent to the studio as an attachment last month, asks for ‘all raw vocal takes, including alternates, for archival and future uses including voice modelling’. Due Friday. Esme's contract says masters and ‘such stems as the Artist agrees in writing’. Nobody asked her.
items.label: Test: what leaves the building — and how much of her voice was ever covered?

items.alt: The control room; Corbin holds a printed contract rider; Esme reads it from across the room, arms folded.

bubbles.text: I didn't write it. I didn't read it until this morning.
Voice modelling. So a machine can sing my songs when I'm tired.

items.prompt: I didn't write the rider. I didn't read it either, until this morning.

options.label: “Then read it with her, now. And tell your label the answer is no until she says yes.”
options.reply: …Okay. I'll take the heat for that. It's the right heat.

options.label: “That's not good enough.”
options.reply: I know. I'm saying it anyway.

options.label: “It's the label's problem.”
options.reply: It's her voice. That makes it everyone's.

items.prompt: The rider wants every raw vocal take by Friday. Esme never agreed. What's the answer?
items.risk: Her voice used for something she never agreed to.
timeout: Friday arrives with the takes still ‘pending’ and the label chasing.

hints.text: Whose voice is it — and what has she actually agreed to?

options.label: Deliver them — the label is paying for the sessions
options.result: Two hundred and twelve takes leave the building.
options.consequence: Paying for a session isn't consent to every use of a voice.
options.fail: Her performances don't leave for new uses without her written yes.

options.label: No, until Esme says yes in writing: only what her contract covers leaves; the raw takes and alternates stay in the building; Esme, her manager and the label settle the rider
options.result: Corbin takes it to the label. Esme's manager takes it to her lawyer. The takes stay on Coldframe's drives.
options.consequence: Her voice, her yes — and the studio holding custody while the owners decide.

options.label: Ask Hollis to decide
options.result: Hollis: “It's not mine to decide either. It's hers.”
options.consequence: Passes the question to someone else who doesn't own it.

options.label: Deliver watermarked copies so any leak can be traced
options.result: Traceable — and still delivered without her consent.
options.fail: Watermarking doesn't make an unconsented copy acceptable.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #99 · AVERY'S LENS  The answer is no until she says yes  A studio holds an artist's performances in trust. Share them with named people for a stated use, record her written consent for anything more, and treat every link as a copy you might not get back.  A review link anyone could open carried an unreleased vocal to eleven addresses — and a contract rider asked for her voice to train a model she'd never agreed to.

items.alt: The share-log sheet rewritten as a custody policy: old link disabled and its log kept for the label's lawyers; review links only for named people, view-only, expiring in seven days; watermarked review copies; raw takes stay in the building; a consent log of Esme's written yes or no per use; every share checked monthly.
items.caption: Custody, written down.

items.title: clause 7 · ‘masters and agreed stems’
items.body: Esme's recording agreement, clause 7: the label may use ‘the masters and such stems as the Artist agrees in writing’. Nothing about raw takes. Nothing about voices. The rider arrived later, as an attachment.

items.prompt: How do her files — and every artist's — leave the building from now on?
unknown: Whether the label accepts the policy
items.risk: The next open link, the next rider.
timeout: The next review link is created with the old defaults.

hints.text: What would stop this for the next artist, not just this one?

items.note: Draft decision (DR-S10E08). Option B needs Authority & access at LIMITED or better — owners who'll sign quickly.

options.label: Leave it to the label's settings
options.result: The next open link is the label's again.
options.consequence: Custody handed to someone else's defaults.

options.label: A custody policy Hollis signs, Esme agrees and the label accepts: named, view-only, expiring review links; watermarked review copies; a consent log per use; raw takes never leave without the artist's written yes; every share checked monthly
options.result: Hollis signs it; Esme signs the consent log; Corbin gets the label to accept it by Friday.
options.consequence: The studio's custody, written down — with the owners on board.

options.label: Pim tightens this album's links; the policy waits
options.result: This album's safe. The next artist starts with the old defaults.
options.consequence: The best you can do when the owners won't sign quickly — and it covers one album.

options.label: Stop using links; courier everything on drives
options.result: Slow, expensive — and a drive can be copied too.
options.consequence: Changes the medium, not the custody.

items.alt: The control room; Esme holds up a signed page of the consent log; Hollis beside her with the custody policy.

bubbles.text: My yes, my no. Line by line. I've never seen one of these before.
Neither had I, in thirty years. Every artist gets one now.

items.alt: The control room; Pim points at the backup status on the screen; Maya leans in.

bubbles.text: The off-site copy says ‘up to date’… as of nineteen days ago.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  A studio holds performances in trust. Every use beyond the artist’s contract needs her own written yes; the answer is no until she says it. Hold custody: named, view-only, expiring links; watermarked review copies; a consent log; a monthly check of every share. When something leaks, stop it, keep the log, measure what you can’t account for, and tell the artist plainly. The label’s lawyers — never the studio — deal with a stranger who has a copy. Not legal advice (RV-179).
REFLECTION (optional)  · What have you been handed in trust that you share more easily than its owner would?
